sources.title: C. Edmund Bosworth, Ghaznavids
sources.note: Direct full text read: foundation, 977 to 1186, successive territorial contraction, 1040 and 1059 settlement. Overview includes separately decoded map warning.

sources.title: C. Edmund Bosworth, Mahmud b. Sebuktegin
sources.note: Indexed original full relevant paragraphs read: expensive army, taxation, temple treasures, captives and Persian administrative officers.

sources.title: C. Edmund Bosworth, Dandanqan
sources.note: Indexed original complete article and PDF: final two historical paragraphs, 23 May 1040, famine/drought and loss of Khorasan.

sources.title: Italian Archaeological Mission, The Ghaznavid Palace
sources.note: Direct project page read: plan, southwest private quarters, decoration, multiple Ghaznavid/Ghurid phases. Do not call all fabric a single 1112 construction.

sources.title: Martina Rugiadi, The Ghaznavid Marble Architectural Decoration: An Overview
sources.note: Direct scholarly PDF read, pages 1 to 3, especially page 2: local quarry, water-system pieces, polychromy, hereditary craft techniques. No use of quoted al-Utbi passage.

sources.title: Association for Iranian Studies, Re-discovering Ghazni: New Data on the Pottery Corpus
sources.note: Original indexed abstract fully read; direct page failed. Reproducible query: site.associationforiranianstudies.org "Re-discovering Ghazni" "manufacture". Abstract includes 11th to 13th-century local glazed/unglazed manufacture and 10th to 13th-century imports; later corpus not conflated with dynasty.

sources.title: Willem Floor, Khwansalar
sources.note: Direct opening paragraph read; restrict to Ghaznavid/Saljuq kitchen department title. Later Safavid/Qajar pantry, food-serving and household details deliberately excluded.

sources.title: Lisa Golombek, Garden vi. Islamic Period
sources.note: Indexed original plus PDF page 2, Ghaznavid paragraphs on streams, Masud I and Balkh bazaar. Not generic later Timurid garden evidence.

sources.title: Gholam-Hosayn Yusofi, Bayhaqi, Abu al-Fazl
sources.note: Direct original Life section reopened and read: Nishapur studies, nineteen years under Abu Nasr Mushkan and fair-copy duties. Individual career, no general literacy rate.

sources.title: J. J. O’Connor and E. F. Robertson, Al-Biruni, MacTutor
sources.note: Direct biography read: 1018 to 1020 Ghazna observations, northern India, Sanskrit translations, study of Indian social customs. Avoid disputed death date and some erroneous dynasty dates in this source.

sources.title: Georges C. Anawati, Biruni v. Pharmacology and Mineralogy
sources.note: Direct original full pharmacology section reopened and read: alphabetical drug entries, multilingual names, synonyms. No current treatment advice or invented public medical access.

sources.title: Dagmar Riedel, Kalila wa Demna i. Redactions and circulation
sources.note: Direct original New Persian translations paragraph reopened and read: Nasr-Allah literary version for Bahramshah combining Arabic verse and Persian prose. Opening animal-fables narrative traditions checked in full article.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum, silver dirham HCR14632
sources.note: Direct object record: reverse inscription محمد رسول الله and translation; Ghazna stated mint, restored dating (41)1 AH / 1020 to 1021, Mahmud and Abbasid al-Qadir; 17.9 mm. Original Arabic copied exactly.

sources.title: C. Edmund Bosworth, Khusrow Malek
sources.note: Direct PDF pages 1 to 3 read: final Punjab phase and Lahore, coalition with Jammu, fall in 581/1185 to 1186, imprisoned ruler and son, subsequent literary testimony. Main dynasty reference conventional endpoint 1186.

proposedOverrides.name: Ghaznavid Emirate
proposedOverrides.summary: Ghazni’s rulers built a military empire whose later territory contracted toward Punjab, while scholarship and skilled crafts flourished.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact existing indexed ID. No aliases or new identity added. No existing runtime card/override or staged parallel bundle found at claim inspection.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Index 1000 to 1279 circa, not dynastic life. Narrative 977 to 1186, Dandanqan 1040, final Lahore phase approximately 1160 onward. End source gives 581/1185 to 1186; dynasty overview conventionally 1186. Period boundaries intentionally circa.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world1000/1100/1200 snapshots retain essentially identical large polygon from 54.8663E to 72.2113E and 28.0731N to 39.8092N. It misses contraction after 1040 and persists after final 1186 conquest. Public opening warns both problems. Full evidence ../identity-all-snapshots.json. No geometry repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Original Arabic exact copied from Ashmolean HCR14632 reverse inscription, matching museum English translation. Dating partly restored (41)1 AH, museum 1020 to 1021; public uses interval, no invented exact point year. Not a reconstructed greeting or everyone’s everyday language.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Pottery includes Ghurid continuation explicitly; no claim House of Lustrewares was Ghaznavid (project attributes it Ghurid). Kitchen uses only period-specific first paragraph. Palace plan is elite household evidence; water fittings are not proof of toilets, universal supply or sanitation. No unsupported healthcare access claims. Map inspection separate from historical sources.
batchIdentityNotes.override: Retain imported from/to as map_coverage, fell null and successors empty pending independent event-target geometry validation.
